sre-oncall: Alert: p95 text-gen latency jumped from 210ms -> 950ms across a subset of hosts in prod.us-east-1 around 17:04 UTC. Rate steady, throughput dropped ~18%. Noticed lots of scale-ups at same time.
sre-oncall: trace id f8c3a1 - spikes correlate with provisioner handoff delays and repeated kernel fallback logs.
Mina: looking at the logs now. saw kernel-selector choose fp16_fast then immediately fall back to int8_quant for same model in same request stream. that smells like probe mismatch.
Raj: can you paste the exact log lines?
Mina: "kernel_match: selected=fp16_fast score=0.87; run_err=kv_cache_miss; fallback=int8_quant score=0.65"
Mina: also saw this stack: "serving/runtime/joiner.go:254: joiner.WaitForKV -> prefetch timeout 120ms"
Cheng: perf profiles attached by perf-bot show long memcpy on GPU when fp16_fast chosen, but int8 path faster. memcpys map to KV fetch stalls.
perf-bot: profile summary (top):
  - 42% time kernel-launch wait (host -> gpu memcpy)
  - 27% time idling on lock: kv_cache.lookup
  - 15% time kernel execution
perf-bot: link: https://perf.internal/plot/f8c3a1 (private)
Olivia: noisy neighbor hypothesis: several co-tenants hit large batch bursts which saturated PCIe on those hosts. autoscaler spun new instances but warm-pool had wrong kernel variant pinned so warm forks took longer to prime.
Raj: which warm-pool config? I remember we set warm_pool.image_tags = ["fp16_fast_v3"] for that fleet.
Mina: yep. but runtime now prefers a different kernel variant at runtime because of sequence length distribution. kernel-selector probe runs at boot and caches match -> mismatch if workload shifts.
Cheng: root cause looks like coupled issues: (1) KV prefetch timeout under contention -> cache miss cascades, (2) kernel-selector probe cache stale -> chooses suboptimal kernel causing long memcpy, (3) autoscaler policy too reactive so we see many cold joins instead of warmfork reuse.
Raj: quick mitigation: 1) bump prefetch timeout from 120ms -> 300ms for us-east-1 temporary, 2) enlarge warm-pool by +15% for the fleet, 3) pin kernel variant to int8_quant for the next 2 hours. thoughts?
Olivia: ok for short window. we should also change autoscale policy: prefer warmfork reuse threshold at 0.6 instead of 0.8 to reduce cold starts.
Mina: applied kernel pin via rollout flag (runtime.kernel.pin=int8_quant) to fleet-12. rolling restart of provisioner scheduled.
sre-oncall: bumped warm-pool size +15% and increased prefetch timeout. monitoring.
Cheng: started a lightweight probe: run 100 synthetic requests with sequence mix; observed p95 drop from 950ms -> 230ms on pinned hosts. good signal.
Raj: create follow-up infra ticket to change kernel-selector probing heuristic: probe on workload shift, not only boot. add TTL for probe cache.
Olivia: logging: please add metric runtime.kernel.fallback.count and kv.prefetch.time_ms histogram to the console dashboard.
Mina: created ticket INFRA-2342 with proposed changes and timeline.
perf-bot: added an automated regression alert for kernel-fallback rate > 0.5% per minute.
sre-oncall: current status — p95 back to normal on most hosts, throughput recovering. keeping this thread open for 2h.
Raj: nice work. postmortem + blameless runbook follow-up pls.
Mina: will own postmortem, assign to Cheng for profiling deep-dive and Olivia for autoscale tuning.
Olivia: adding runbook note: if p95 > 600ms and kernel-fallback > 1% then pin kernel variant + scale warm-pool, ramp prefetch.
sre-oncall: thanks all :thumbsup: will update if anything else pops up.
